rationale: The Latin anchor *Cerdāci lítus* (lítus = "shore, coast") unambiguously confirms a geographical sense of land along the edge of a body of water, matching shore.n.01. The place-name "Cerdices óra" (Cerdic's shore/landing place) refers to a coastal location in the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle, entirely ruling out the structural-support sense of shore.n.02.
